title: Call to Bind Ourselves to Christ
english: …my son, you went up” (Genesis 49:9). And the nations were bound fast in Him, never to be loosed. So let us too be bound to Christ, never to be loosed. If we strive at all to be saved and to profit from His feasts, He in turn will raise us together with Lazarus from our dead works (Hebrews 9:14), the works done without Him.

So let us dine with Him in Bethany (John 12:2), which means “house of obedience”; so let us fittingly gather our thoughts, together with the senses of the body, out of the captivity of forgetfulness, crying out and saying: “Hosanna in the highest; blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord” (Matthew 21:9), who comes to enter His own Jerusalem, not to suffer as He did then, but to save her and to be glorified by her, as David calls out to her, saying: “Extol the Lord, O Jerusalem; praise your God, O Zion” (Psalm 147:12).
He said it twice, “extol” and “praise,” with soul and body, “for He has strengthened the bars of your gates” (Psalm 147:13), which are faith, hope, love…
translator_notes: The section opens by completing Genesis 49:9 from the previous section, and the list of the bars of the gates runs on into the next section.
“Extol” and “praise” render two different Greek verbs in Psalm 147:12; Hesychius takes the pair to mean praise with soul and with body.
“House of obedience” is the traditional explanation of the name Bethany.
Psalm 147:12–13 is Psalm 147:1–2 in the Septuagint.
